**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Section 13 satisfies the LICENSE rule at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback:

- **§13.1** — subscription grant runs directly to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf," worldwide and non-exclusive, with Authorized User sublicensing. Affiliates/contractors are in scope from the outset, so the fallback's "on written notice" mechanic is unnecessary.
- **§13.2** — paid-up software and Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables are licensed to Customer and its Affiliates on a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" basis, including modification, derivative works, and contractor support. §14.3 confirms this perpetual licence covers Vendor Technology required to use a Deliverable.
- **§13.3** — transfer permitted to an Affiliate or successor via §24 (which allows M&A/successor assignment without Vendor consent), and revocation/suspension is limited to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity.

No "revocable" language or at-will revocation right appears, and the §13.4 restrictions are standard, carving out lawful reverse engineering, authorized security testing, and use of Customer Data and output.
